summary.headline: Advait Energy Q2 FY27 revenue rose 40.8% YoY to INR 221 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.5% and order book at INR 1,575 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 221 crore (up 40.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 32 crore (up 84.4%) and PAT INR 19 crore (up 88.5%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 400 crore (up 45.4%) with PAT of INR 34 crore. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 55-60% (above INR 1,000 crore) and a long-term INR 5,000 crore revenue ambition. Debt-to-equity rose to 0.86x from 0.42x at March 2026, and an equity raise is planned for Q3 or Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +84.4% YoY; margin vs 11% in Q2 FY26
+88.5% YoY vs INR 10 crore; margin vs 6.5%
+77.9% YoY vs INR 19 crore; margin vs 6.9%

financial_highlights.metric: Order book (incl. L1) as on 30 Sep 2026

segments.name: Power Transmission Solutions (PTS)
segments.commentary: Order book mix about 60-65% PTS vs 35% NRE; PTS EBITDA margin described as steady over four years. Recent orders include about INR 52 crore from DGVCL and multiple PGVCL orders, plus ERS, OPGW and stringing tools.

segments.name: New & Renewable Energy (NRE)
segments.commentary: Management guides NRE EBITDA margin of 7-8% to build 30-50% over two years, driven by manufacturing. Current solar and green hydrogen EPC margins are cited at 5-8%; a 150 MW / 300 MWh standalone BESS order in Junagadh, Gujarat was secured. A 100 MW solar EPC order from KP Group targets 8-10% EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 55-60% YoY, crossing INR 1,000 crore; H2 FY27 needs about INR 700 crore (about INR 325-350 crore per quarter), which management says is on track.

Group EBITDA margin: management says it is looking for similar levels to H1 (about 14%) in H2 FY27, but declined to use the word 'committing'; group margin targeted at 15% once manufacturing is established, with 1-1.5% annual improvement meanwhile.

Long-term: INR 5,000 crore revenue target over about 5 years; manufacturing share of sales targeted at 70-75% by FY28-29 (other comment: 65-75% by FY28-29/FY29-30); NRE and PTS targeted at roughly 50:50 contribution in 2-3 years.
Capex: FY27 guidance of INR 300-350 crore; INR 101 crore incurred in H1 and about INR 140 crore planned in H2.
Target debt-to-equity for manufacturing and solutions business of about 0.5-0.7x; equity raise planned for Q3 or Q4 FY27 to fund working capital.
capex_capacity: Gangad, Gujarat integrated manufacturing facility: Phase 1 operational by Q4 FY27 across PTS and NRE.
2.5 GWh BESS manufacturing facility (expandable to 5 GWh): final plant and machinery orders placed; operational by Q4 FY27. Management guides 40-60% utilisation in year one.

Electrolyser: 30 MW assembly line inaugurated March 2026; first 1 MW unit being assembled in-house for engineering development. Management plans 150 MW operational around Q4 FY27 (within a 300 MW Phase 2), with capacity expandable to 1 GW by 2028-29.
Completed electrolyser projects: 300 kW for THDC (Rishikesh) and a 1 MW EPC and supply project in Gujarat, expected to be commissioned in the current quarter.
Fuel cell: INR 22 crore investment linked to a technology licence with AVL and TECO; management promised a sizeable update next quarter, including a timeline for the first plant.
demand_pricing: Order book split about 60-65% public and 40% private; management says collection cycles in public and private have been equally efficient.
Order book mix by execution: about 60-62% EPC and about 38% manufacturing; target 70-75% manufacturing from FY28-29.
New order inflow for next year expected 50:50 PTS and NRE; management expects order book at least 1.6-1.8x last year's revenue.

Revenue potential: 150 MW electrolyser capacity cited at INR 600-1,000 crore; BESS at about INR 1,000-1,100 crore per GWh at full utilisation. PTS full-capacity manufacturing sales above INR 2,500 crore.

Management said over 13 Indian green hydrogen players engaged through the 5 MW live testing programme and cited an active electrolyser inquiry pipeline above 1 GW. It also said Chinese equipment is excluded from public tenders and some Japan/Europe-backed projects.

qa_highlights.question: What gives conviction in the INR 5,000 crore revenue target over about 5 years (about 7x FY26)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 50-60% revenue and EBITDA CAGR over the past 6-7 years and said the company is now qualified for larger product and project sizes; it did not break down the drivers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the public vs private mix in the INR 1,575 crore order book and how does it affect collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 60-65% public and 40% private; collection cycles in public have been as efficient as private over the last 3-4 years. Exact figures to follow via CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PTS margin fall while NRE margin rose?
qa_highlights.answer: PTS margin has been steady for four years with about 1.5% annual change; NRE margin is improving and is guided up 30-50% over two years, driven by manufacturing and solutions.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the INR 22 crore TECO investment and its status, given TECO's reported bankruptcy filing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a licence-linked investment for fuel cell technology with AVL and TECO for about a decade, not an equity stake in the company. It promised an update next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Ind-AS 115 adjusted core revenue and EBITDA, and the gap between NRE revenue of about INR 4 crore and EBIT of INR 7.8 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Core manufacturing EBITDA is 17-18% standalone; NRE EPC EBITDA is 5-7%. Management said the operating profit is from operational revenue only, with margins varying order to order (6-8%). No reconciliation was provided.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR 1,100 crore and the 14% margin still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the track is in line, with H2 growth of 55-60%, and that inflation was partly covered by pre-booked raw materials. It would not call 14% a commitment, but expects similar numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and capital structure plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Target D/E of 0.5-0.7x for the manufacturing and solutions business; asset-creation business model may shift leverage. Equity raise planned for Q3 or Q4 FY27 for working capital.

qa_highlights.question: What is the electrolyser order pipeline and when does the 300 MW Phase 2 come on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: No electrolyser orders yet booked from the 30 MW line; 150 MW expected operational around Q4 FY27 given an active inquiry above 1 GW, with orders above 150 MW targeted for FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost basis of the AGPL share purchase (INR 6,250 vs INR 25,000 per share)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the figure and referred the question to the CFO by email. AGPL requires funding backed by AETL.

qa_highlights.question: What is expected utilisation and revenue for the 2.5 GWh BESS plant, and how does it reconcile with the INR 5,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Year-one utilisation of 40-60%, with the mix of captive and open-market orders not split. Management said the INR 5,000 crore target is the base case and that capital allocation and cash flow will set the pace.

risks_watch: Electrolyser: the 30 MW line had no booked orders as of the call; the 150 MW Q4 FY27 start depends on converting a >1 GW inquiry pipeline.
Balance sheet: D/E rose to 0.86x from 0.42x, and borrowings of INR 280 crore; the planned equity raise in Q3 or Q4 FY27 is pending.
Margin: H2 inflation risk to the 14% EBITDA margin; NRE EPC margins of 5-8% are well below the core manufacturing 17-18%.
Execution: H1 executed orders of about INR 400 crore against a H2 requirement of about INR 700 crore to reach INR 1,100 crore.
Disclosure gaps: no exact order-book product split, no AGPL deal value, no reconciliation of NRE revenue vs EBIT, and the TECO investment remains unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the manufacturing transition, but evasive on several specifics: it deferred exact order-book splits, the AGPL deal value and the NRE revenue/EBIT gap to email follow-up, and declined to commit to the 14% margin.

So we are looking forward to have similar numbers.
We are not looking forward to put out the entire 300-MW capacity to be operational in 2027.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of 55-60% (above INR 1,000 crore) reiterated, requiring about INR 325-350 crore per quarter in H2; backed by a 47% YoY order book of about INR 1,575 crore and new plants (Gangad, 2.5 GWh BESS, 150 MW electrolyser) guided to go live around Q4 FY27, though only the order book is quantified and the plants are not yet running.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 14.2% with management looking for similar ~14% in H2 but declining to commit; group margin target 15% once manufacturing is established, and 1-1.5% annual improvement meanwhile; H2 inflation risk noted.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gangad Phase 1 (PTS and NRE), 2.5 GWh BESS plant (plant and machinery orders placed) and 150 MW electrolyser within Phase 2 are all guided operational around Q4 FY27, with capex of INR 140 crore planned in H2 FY27 against INR 101 crore spent in H1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth of 55-60% (above INR 1,000 crore) reiterated, needing about INR 700 crore in H2 (INR 325-350 crore per quarter) versus INR 400 crore in H1; order book about INR 1,575 crore, up 47% YoY, with execution described as on track.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR 300-350 crore with INR 140 crore planned in H2, and a fuel cell update with a first-plant timeline promised next quarter; the INR 22 crore fuel cell investment is licence-linked and the capex plan is already set.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is reiterating rather than raising FY27 growth of 55-60%, and the H2 requirement of about INR 700 crore is already a stretch against H1 of INR 400 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs about INR 700 crore to hit INR 1,100 crore, the electrolyser line has no booked orders, and the 14% margin is not committed; D/E rose to 0.86x with an equity raise pending in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fuel cell technology update with a first-plant timeline promised next quarter, and the 150 MW electrolyser and 2.5 GWh BESS start-ups are guided for Q4 FY27; the 1 MW in-house unit is already being assembled.

rows.label: Electrolyser order conversion from >1 GW inquiry pipeline
rows.why: No electrolyser orders yet booked from the 30 MW line, while 150 MW is targeted around Q4 FY27 and orders above 150 MW are targeted for FY27-28 against a pipeline above 1 GW.

rows.label: Equity raise for working capital in Q3/Q4 FY27
rows.why: Equity raise is planned to fund working capital as D/E rose to 0.86x from 0.42x on INR 280 crore gross borrowings, against a target of 0.5-0.7x for the manufacturing business.

rows.label: NRE margin ramp to 30-50% over two years
rows.why: NRE EPC margins are 5-8% today, with a 100 MW KP Group solar EPC order targeting 8-10% EBITDA; the ramp depends on manufacturing coming online.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 55-60% FY27 growth, the Gangad, BESS and electrolyser start-ups around Q4 FY27 and the manufacturing shift, but deferred the order-book split, AGPL deal value, NRE revenue/EBIT gap and TECO investment details to follow-up, and declined to commit to the 14% margin.
